title: Education Benefits and the Sponsor's Disability Compensation Award, Benefit Level Changes and Supplemental Payments
content:
Holding Disability Compensation shapes eligibility under Education Benefits (GI Bill and Dependents' Education). The rules below set out where the two meet, and the limits on the supplemental education payments.

**Chapter 35 and the sponsor's award.** Chapter 35 is established for a child or spouse only while the sponsor's Disability Compensation award is permanent and total, or where the sponsor died of a service-connected cause. A child paid Chapter 35 for a term cannot be recognized as a school child on the sponsor's compensation award for the same months.

| Sponsor's situation | Chapter 35 may be established |
|---|---|
| Award permanent and total | Yes |
| Sponsor died of a service-connected cause | Yes |

**Post-9/11 benefit level.** A Post-9/11 GI Bill benefit level rises when added qualifying active service moves the aggregate service into a higher band. A 30-day continuous period of service ending in a service-connected disability discharge qualifies for the 100 percent level.

**Transfer to dependents.** Transfer of entitlement to dependents is available only on tiers that allow it (the Post-9/11 GI Bill levels) and is requested by the service member through the Department of Defense, never on a VA service call.

**Supplemental payments.** A student moving from a highly rural county to attend school receives the rural relocation benefit once ($500.00 on the Post-9/11 levels). Tutorial assistance, licensing test reimbursement and the STEM Scholarship extension are paid within their tier limits — $100.00 a month and $1200.00 over the life of the benefit for tutorial assistance, $2000.00 for one licensing or certification test, and 9 months up to $30000.00 for the STEM Scholarship on the Post-9/11 levels.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A child in a fall term paid under Chapter 35 is not also recognized as a school child on the parent's compensation award for September through December of that term.
